text: Future feature (deferred from 2026-08-16 dark-Stage deliberation on 5D98DBCC): cross-workspace shared read-only serving WITHOUT relaxing workspace containment. The external-path read-sources.yaml design was rejected on NON-NEGOTIABLE Principle III/IV grounds (see docs/decisions/2026-08-16-shared-external-readonly-databases-deliberation.md). Constitution-compliant alternative (Option C): run one graphtor-docs serve process rooted where the shared db legitimately lives and let other dev workspaces consume it as MCP clients. Requires a multiplexing MCP transport (HTTP/SSE or local socket) beyond today's 1:1 STDIO, and structurally eliminates the F6 concurrent-multi-process-file gap. Must carry its own Constitution Check (III + V + authz/exfiltration for the network surface) when planned. Also encompasses truly closing the F6 cross-process read-only ownership/liveness window (deferred from spike 970AE45A). Operator confirmation needed on whether to pursue.

Adversarial review of 047-S surfaced a PRE-EXISTING .gitignore hygiene issue, unrelated to 047-S: a duplicate ".engram/" blanket-ignore entry exists later in the file (around the "# UE" section) that overrides earlier deliberate negations (!.engram/.version, !.engram/.workspace-id, !.engram/config.toml, !.engram/registry.yaml), silently excluding those config files from version control despite the negations intending to keep them tracked. Confirmed via diff against main (33bbb37) that 047-S's stowaway .gitignore change only added .copilot-tracking/ and .graphtor/config/sources.yaml entries; it did not introduce this duplicate .engram/ line. Recommend removing the later duplicate ".engram/" line (or confirming intent and removing the stale negations if .engram/ config files are meant to stay untracked).

Adversarial review of 047-S surfaced a minor model-routing config drift inherited from the dark-factory-stowaways-047-S stash content (not introduced by 047-S itself, and not something Ship should silently rewrite beyond what the operator authorized to carry over): .autoharness/config.yaml declares model_routing.tier2.reasoning_effort: "high", but .github/agents/.ship.agent.md's frontmatter declares reasoning_effort: "xhigh" (only "orchestrator" is configured for "xhigh" in config.yaml). Separately, .autoharness/config.yaml's adversarial_review.alt_provider/alt_family (google/gemini-2.5-pro) were enabled by the same stowaway, but the consuming .github/agents/subagents/adversarial-review.agent.md frontmatter and .github/instructions/adversarial-review.instructions.md prose were NOT updated to match (the instructions file still states "Not currently configured for this workspace") — those two files were outside 047-S's explicitly authorized 6-file stowaway scope. ADDITIONALLY (found by Copilot review on PR #97, cycle 4): .github/agents/_orchestrator.agent.md's frontmatter now declares model_family: "gpt-5.6-sol" but the SAME file's own prose (default-model table / configuration example, ~lines 347 and 360-361) still names the prior "gpt-5.4" value, so the checked-in agent's documentation contradicts its own frontmatter after the stowaway change. Recommend a small chore pass (via Stage, not Ship) to reconcile: (a) Ship's reasoning_effort to config.yaml's declared tier2 value or add an explicit override, (b) regenerate/update adversarial-review.agent.md + adversarial-review.instructions.md so the alt-provider wiring is fully consistent end-to-end, and (c) update _orchestrator.agent.md's own default-model-table prose to match its new gpt-5.6-sol frontmatter.

Optional, non-blocking follow-up from 047-S (read-only serve guarantee honesty) adversarial review: src/main.rs's open_serve_databases doc comment references "the engine/filesystem-enforced read-only primitive proven in P1-T0 (050.009-T)" without an explicit F6 (best-effort under multiple independent guards on one file, same- or cross-process) pointer, unlike the five other surfaces this shipment corrected (ENGINE_READONLY_OPEN_LOG_MESSAGE constant, open_engine_readonly rustdoc, is_engine_enforced_readonly rustdoc, EngineReadonlyGuard struct doc, and the design doc). This is NOT an overstated claim (confirmed by direct review — it references the primitive by name rather than independently asserting a guarantee), so it did not require correction under 047-S's "correct overstated wording" scope, but adding a one-line F6 cross-reference there would complete the coupling for a future reader who only reads main.rs. Low priority, cosmetic.

Optional further F6 wording refinement surfaced by Copilot review cycle 4 on PR #97 (047-S), after 3+ review-fix cycles had already substantially improved the honesty of the read-only guarantee wording: the current phrasing "independently guarded more than once" (in ENGINE_READONLY_OPEN_LOG_MESSAGE, is_engine_enforced_readonly/open_engine_readonly/open_sqlite_readonly rustdocs, the EngineReadonlyGuard struct doc, and the design doc's Read-only serve hardening section) technically also captures purely SEQUENTIAL opens (guard A fully drops before guard B ever locks the same file), which do NOT trigger the F6 restore-ordering problem since a fully-completed prior guard's Drop always runs before the next guard's lock captures a fresh "current" state. The precise failure condition is OVERLAPPING guard lifetimes (same- or cross-process), not merely "guarded more than once" over the file's lifetime. Reviewed and deliberately NOT applied as a 4th+ round fix on 047-S: after 3 substantive review-fix cycles the finding count went 9 -> 4 -> 2 -> 10 (non-convergent), indicating diminishing/negative returns on further precision-chasing for a residual (F6) that is explicitly documented as a known best-effort limitation rather than something requiring formal edge-case-complete specification. If desired, a future pass could reword the qualifier from "independently guarded more than once" to "guarded by overlapping independent lifetimes" across all five surfaces, and could also clarify that after an overlap ends, the final restored permissions equal whichever guard captured/restored last, which may or may not match the pre-overlap state (rather than "not guaranteed to end up writable").

docs/memory/2026-08-17/047-s-session-closure-memory.md's "This PR itself went through N Copilot review passes" framing is self-referentially unstable (each fix to N creates pass N+1, chased across PR #99 review rounds 4-5). Optional cleanup: reword to cover both fixed and explicitly deferred findings without a precise pass-count — for example, "This PR went through several Copilot review passes; all but one finding were fixed directly, and the remaining finding (a self-referential pass-count drift) was deliberately deferred as a follow-up rather than chased indefinitely" — the next time this file is touched. Do NOT use a blanket "each promptly addressed" phrasing: that would overclaim, since the final pass's finding was explicitly deferred (stashed here), not fixed.
